newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS HUNT HISTORY, SPRINGBOKS CONSISTENCY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS HUNT HISTORY, SPRINGBOKS CONSISTENCY.

text.p: The British Lions have already wrapped up the series against South Africa but history is against them competing a 3-0 sweep in the third test on Saturday.
The Springboks have not been defeated at Ellis Park for four years and six matches.

The last side to beat them here was France in 1993 and that was by a single point. Even Sean Fitzpatrick's brilliant All Blacks of 1996 went down to the Springboks 32-22 the last time a test was played here.

The all-conquering Lions of 1974 were also unable to defeat South Africa at Ellis Park. Irish flanker Fergus Slattery thought he had scored the winning try on that occasion but the referee did not award it and the match ended 13-13.

Another Irishman, injured hooker Keith Wood, is well aware of the importance of the occasion. "Our initial objective was to win the series, so in the first two tests it was a case of just hoping to God that we win," he said.
"But now that we are on the threshold of a whitewash everyone has focused in on the possibility of creating history by winning 3-0."
Wood, a key figure for the Lions in the tests, will be in the stands on Saturday, along with fellow injury victims Alan Tait and Gregor Townsend.
But the squad ethic has come through strongly at the end of a tour noted for its 'one for all, all for one' attitude.

English wing Tony Underwood summed it up: "I am desperate to become part of the history we are going out to create at Ellis Park but no more keen than I was before the teams were selected for the previous two tests."
Springbok skipper Gary Teichmann has the task of lifting his beaten team against the highly confident Lions but does not imagine this will be a problem.

"I don't think it'll be very difficult at all. I think we've got something to prove. I believe we played well last week and, if we can just keep getting better and better, then it augurs well for the Tri-Nations," he said.
"The guys were obviously a bit down as it would have been great to be one-all now. But we've accepted it and now we just want to play on Saturday and prove that we can win".
With two new caps in the side and two more winning their second caps Teichmann knows the pressure is on.
"Johan (Erasmus) was with us a bit last year on the tour overseas so he's quite happy. He knows what's going on. He's a great player and I'm sure he'll come through pretty well.
"Jannie (de Beer), I think, has fitted in well. He played before with some of the guys and he played with Joost back in 1992."

De Beer is the key man for the Springboks. He has answered the call for a reliable place-kicker but a career kicking record of 50 percent reveals how much of a gamble it is for coach Carel du Plessis to prefer him to the battle-hardened Henry Honiball.

The late withdrawal of Boeta Wessels with a quadricep injury has allowed Honiball to return to the bench. But Andre Joubert, the nation's most-capped full-back, has been ruled out with a groin strain.
Under the circumstances the Ellis Park bogey may not be enough to save the Springboks from a humiliating whitewash.
Teams:

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Johan Erasmus, 5-Krynauw Otto, 4-Hannes Strdom, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-James Dalton, 1-Os du Randt.

British Lions - 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-John Bentley, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Matt Dawson; 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Neil Back, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Martin Johnson (captain), 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Tom Smith.
